# A cross-reference target that names an entry this document has

The twin of the dangling-target probe: here every target resolves, so the
dangling-target report must be silent in every format. A check that only ever
saw the dangling fixture would pass just as happily on a filter that reported
every target, which is why this file exists.

Three resolution shapes, which are the whole of the rule.

An exact single-level match — the target is a top-level entry this document
marks: [robins]{.index entry="Robins"} is marked, and
[wrens]{.index entry="Wrens" see="Robins"} points at it.

A multi-level path match — the target names every level of a deeper entry:
[barn owls]{.index entry="Birds!Owls!Barn"} is marked, and
[finches]{.index entry="Finches" see="Birds!Owls!Barn"} points at the whole
path.

A match against a level that exists only as the PARENT of a deeper entry. No
mark writes `Trees!Oak` as an entry of its own, but the index has that level
because a deeper entry hangs from it, and a reader following the target lands
there: [acorns]{.index entry="Trees!Oak!Acorn"} is marked, and
[sap]{.index entry="Sap" see-also="Trees!Oak"} points at its parent.

::: {.qi-index-here}
:::
